## 固定收益開盤主論述

伊朗戰爭帶來的近期通膨威脅隨油價再度下跌而減輕，但美國公債6月12日收盤仍小幅走弱。2年期殖利率上升1.9個基點至4.082%，5年期上升2.2個基點至4.207%，10年期上升1.9個基點至4.481%，30年期則小升1.2個基點至4.968%。這波走勢收回前一交易日部分漲幅，但全週殖利率仍下跌，其中2年期下降6.6個基點，10年期下降5個基點。

本日最鮮明的特徵，是美國公債市場不願只憑外交樂觀情緒延續早盤的全球債券漲勢。隨著美國與伊朗更接近就荷莫茲海峽達成協議，WTI下跌3.23%至$84.88，布蘭特原油下跌3.37%至$87.33。歐洲短天期公債強勁上漲，英國2年期殖利率下降14個基點至4.20%，德國2年期殖利率下跌近10個基點至2.58%。美國公債起初也跟進，但投資人仍認為聯準會再次升息的機率不低，並等待Kevin Warsh就任主席後首次主持會議，漲勢因而消退。

美國收盤結構顯示阻力所在。10年期實質殖利率僅下降0.1個基點至2.151%，幾乎持平；10年期損益兩平通膨率卻上升2個基點至2.33%。現貨原油走低並未再度壓低長期通膨補償。2年期與10年期利差持平於39.9個基點，2年期與30年期利差僅收窄0.7個基點至88.6個基點。各天期票息債殖利率近乎平行上升，反映的是政策疑慮延續，而非長端新一輪財政或期限溢價衝擊。

美國消費者數據稍微減輕聯準會壓力，卻不足以解除警報。密西根大學6月消費者信心初值由44.8升至48.9，1年期通膨預期由4.8%降至4.6%，長期通膨預期則由3.9%降至3.4%。當前狀況與預期均廣泛改善，但通膨讀數的絕對水準仍高。另一項經濟學家調查把首次降息的預測中位數延後至2027年6月，市場定價則繼續反映聯準會在2026年底前升息的機率很高。

能源價格回落及外交解決的可能性提振風險資產。標普500指數上漲0.50%，那斯達克100指數上漲0.64%，費城半導體指數上漲1.52%，VIX則下跌9.05%至17.68。SpaceX規模創紀錄的$750億首次公開募股，開盤價較每股$135的發行價高11%，掛牌首日收高19%，進一步顯示股票投資人對科技與人工智慧曝險的需求仍具韌性。美元指數下跌0.11%。

跨資產訊號並非一致反映市場已經放心。黃金上漲3.05%至$4,215，投資級債券基金價格小幅下跌，高收益債基金則大致持平。這種組合顯示，投資人願意降低最迫切的能源與波動率溢價，卻不認為地緣政治或通膨前景已經塵埃落定。

這項區別在美東時間17:00固定收益市場截止後更顯重要。巴基斯坦總理夏巴茲・夏立夫表示，美國與伊朗已同意立即且永久停止軍事行動，並預定6月19日在瑞士正式簽署協議；據稱美國總統Donald Trump也準備解除海上封鎖。這項宣布使外交進展大幅向前，但消息出現在債市收盤後，不可能是週五殖利率變動的原因。接下來須觀察停火能否落實、荷莫茲海峽是否實際重啟，以及協議條款能否持久。

## 油價壓力緩解，聯準會政策溢價仍在

美國公債早盤上漲，源於外交局勢再度轉向和解。Trump先前曾揚言採取更多軍事行動，之後改稱協議已接近達成；官員則表示，雙方正就重開荷莫茲海峽的臨時安排進行談判。布蘭特原油在歐洲交易時段跌破$86，為3個月來首次。當時美國2年期殖利率據報下降約2個基點至接近4.05%，但日線歷史資料的最終讀數為4.082%。

收盤前走勢反轉，顯示利率市場正在區分未來能源衝擊減弱，與已經反映在物價及政策預期中的通膨。前一日生產者物價報告顯示供應鏈成本廣泛上升，5月消費者物價年增率也已達4.2%。週五原油下跌改善了未來整體通膨展望，卻無法逆轉已實現的漲價，也未釐清企業將把多少成本轉嫁給消費者。

密西根大學調查提供較有利的當前訊號。消費者信心指數上升4.1點至48.9；當前狀況由45.8升至48.4，預期指數由44.1升至49.3，月初汽油價格壓力減輕，改善了家庭對個人財務與企業狀況的看法。1年期通膨預期下降0.2個百分點，長期預期的降幅更大，達0.5個百分點。

家庭通膨預期會影響薪資要求與定價行為，因此其下降對聯準會具有意義，但目前水準仍不足以證明能源衝擊已從消費者心理中消失。1年期預期仍達4.6%，遠高於聯準會目標；信心改善也削弱了「高通膨伴隨需求突然崩跌」的解讀。

雇主薪酬數據提供了另一項勞動成本觀察，但仍未解決政策爭論。3月文職受僱者平均每小時薪酬為$49.32，其中工資與薪資為$33.72，福利為$15.60；去年12月三者分別為$48.78、$33.45及$15.33。私人產業平均薪酬為$46.60，包括$32.60的工資與$14.01的福利，高於去年12月的總薪酬$46.15。這些數字反映薪酬水準，而非僱用成本指數衡量的成長率，但仍顯示工資與福利對雇主都是可觀成本。

在彼此拉扯的訊號下，6月16日至17日FOMC會議的焦點不在普遍預期的當次決策，而在下一步的政策傾向。對35名經濟學家的調查顯示，預測中位數為2027年6月及12月各降息一次，使目標區間降至3%-3.25%。3月的前次調查中，受訪者原本預期會在2026年透過降息抵達相同水準。只有3名經濟學家預測今年升息，與持續偏向升息的期貨定價形成對比。

對眼前這次會議，市場共識則高得多。經濟學家與投資人幾乎都預期聯準會把利率維持在3.50%-3.75%，71%的受訪經濟學家預期決議將獲一致通過。更重要的問題，是官員會否保留暗示降息機率高於升息的措辭。四分之三受訪者預期，FOMC將刪除這項寬鬆傾向，或改用下一次調整可能朝任一方向發展的中性表述。

市場對風險的排序已大幅改變。82%的受訪經濟學家認為通膨比失業更危險，沒有人把勞動市場視為較大風險；去年12月則有逾半數受訪者較重視就業。這種轉變解釋了油價及家庭通膨預期下降為何只帶來短暫的債市漲勢：現在必須由後續數據證明物價壓力擴散已經停止。

市場參與者比經濟學家的預測中位數更偏鷹派。高盛美國利率產品共同主管Muhammad Qubbaj表示，經濟活動具韌性、物價上升，以及企業人工智慧支出熱潮，都支持目前的利率定價。交易員認為年底前升息的機率約為75%，並已完全反映2027年3月前升息一次。Warsh主持的首次會議，被視為他能否在分歧的委員會內建立共識，同時強調控制通膨的考驗。

收盤時的殖利率曲線並未顯示升息觀點大幅升溫。2年期與10年期殖利率同樣上升1.9個基點，30年期升幅更小。然而，油價帶動的漲勢未能維持，說明市場已不再認為每一則外交利多都足以消除政策溢價。停火可以減弱下一波通膨衝擊，卻無法單獨判斷目前聯邦基金利率對一個就業、消費支出及資本投資仍然穩健的經濟體是否已具足夠限制性。

前一交易日地緣政治消息帶動市場大漲後，美國公債現券交易也降溫。FINRA記錄到340,363筆交易，面額合計$8,930億，較6月11日減少24.8%。名目票息債交易面額下降20.8%至$7,341億，20年以上天期交易則減少39.6%。成交數據無法判斷投資人買賣方向，但顯示本日小幅賣壓發生在交易較清淡的盤勢，而非又一輪異常活躍的重新定價。

## 歐洲短端大漲，政策爭論反而更棘手

歐洲政府公債對油價下跌的反應比美國公債更強，因為能源衝擊已成為歐洲央行與英國央行政策判斷的當前主軸。短端領漲，英國2年期殖利率下降14個基點，德國2年期殖利率下跌近10個基點。歐洲央行升息25個基點後，交易員下修連續升息的預期；英國市場定價則轉向11月前僅升息一次。

這波債市上漲並不代表市場否定歐洲央行的決策。歐元區5月通膨升至3.2%，基礎物價壓力也增強，官員因此把存款利率上調至2.25%。週五的新訊息在於，油價下跌可能降低快速連續升息的必要性，但決策官員仍警告，衝擊已從能源項目擴散出去。

德國央行總裁Joachim Nagel表示，如有必要，歐洲央行已準備在7月再度升息。他認為高能源成本正影響其他物價及核心通膨，因此即使地緣政治局勢迅速改善，6月升息仍有必要。國際貨幣基金同樣假設2026年將累計升息50個基點，理由是整體與核心通膨可能到2028年仍高於2%。

斯洛伐克央行總裁Peter Kazimir更明確主張利率仍需上調。他表示，即使達成和平協議，受損的生產能力及更廣泛的通膨傳導仍可能延續，物價壓力不會立刻回到目標。6月核心通膨數據或將決定升息時點，但他也指出，決策官員對7月行動尚無共識，9月還會取得新一輪預測。

法國的Emmanuel Moulin則界定了傳導目前所到之處。油氣價格上漲已開始影響其他商品與服務，包括服務籃子中的部分項目，但他尚未看到透過薪資形成的第二輪效應，也不支持預先設定利率路徑。這項區分使歐洲央行有理由因應物價壓力擴散，同時不必假定最持久的薪資—物價機制已經形成。

斯洛維尼亞央行總裁Primoz Dolenc釋出較審慎的政策訊號。他表示，在硬數據顯示通膨上升、成長轉弱後，6月升息確有必要，但目前這一步已經足夠，並未暗示下一次決策方向。依其評估，即使荷莫茲海峽迅速重開，原油也不會立即流通至整條供應鏈。

政策爭議因此在於行動速度，而非能源衝擊是否重要。Nagel與Kazimir強調通膨的持續性，以及保留再度升息的選項；Dolenc與Moulin則主張逐次會議判斷，並指出部分第二輪效應尚未出現。油價下跌後，市場下修預期升息幅度，但仍反映歐洲央行至少再升息一次，且2027年上半年以前再升一次的機率仍具分量。

成長風險使這條政策路徑更難維持。英國4月GDP在3月成長0.3%後萎縮0.1%，為2025年8月以來首次月減。服務業下滑0.2%，生產持平，營建業則成長0.1%。較長期趨勢仍較穩健：截至4月的3個月產出成長0.7%，高於截至3月3個月的0.6%。單月萎縮削弱近期展望，但尚不能證明先前擴張已全面反轉。

英國家庭通膨預期卻朝相反方向發展。未來1年通膨預期中位數由2月的3.2%升至4.0%；再下一個12個月的預期由3.2%升至3.5%，5年期預期由3.7%升至3.9%。家庭感受的當前通膨則由4.6%升至5.0%。

利率看法的變化同樣顯著：53%的家庭預期未來1年利率上升，高於2月的30%；23%預期不變，11%預期下降。單月產出轉弱而通膨預期上升，正好呈現英國央行在6月18日會議前的兩難。油價下跌改善前景，但家庭調查顯示，先前的衝擊已經改變預期。

英國央行總裁Andrew Bailey週末為主動出售英國公債辯護，為政策討論加入資產負債表因素。他表示，若觀察整段期間，量化寬鬆及其逆轉對納稅人整體大致中性：政府自2022年底以來向央行移轉約£1,080億，此前則曾收到近£1,240億的獲利。Bailey反對暫停出售，認為縮小資產負債表可恢復未來發生衝擊時買進資產的空間。即使貨幣政策委員會把銀行利率維持在3.75%，持續主動出售公債仍會收緊金融情勢。

## 信用需求偏好短天期風險與優先順位債權

油價下跌改善歐洲信用市場的整體氣氛，投資人解除部分戰時避險部位，但新融資交易顯示需求仍具選擇性。能提供較短天期、較高償債順位或明確殖利率溢酬的借款人較容易取得資金；涉及較低品質借款人或流動性不確定的結構，仍受到更嚴格檢視。

Lloyds Banking Group發行¥750億、約合$4.68億的日圓計價武士債，為2年來首次進入這個市場。截至6月12日止的本財政年度，外國發行人在日本的發債規模已達¥5,030億，為2015年同期發行¥5,380億以來最高。

日本投資人偏好武士債，原因是其天期通常較同類本國債券短、利差較寬，在日本政策利率上升之際形成具吸引力的組合。由於日本基準殖利率仍低於美國與歐洲，即使計入換匯成本，日圓融資對外國發行人也可能保持競爭力。

Lloyds其中一檔分券為6年期、滿5年可贖回，定價較交換利率高78個基點。標普評等僅高一級的三井住友銀行，4月發行2031年到期債券時，利差為交換利率加28個基點。兩者相差50個基點，為日本買方承擔外國銀行曝險提供明確補償，也讓Lloyds得以運用日本龐大的國內儲蓄資金。

擔保貸款憑證基金呈現更大的結構性轉變。2026年以來，美國CLO ETF淨流入超過$90億，高於去年同期的近$70億。僅6月第一週便流入約$7.4億，為2月初以來最大單週流入。Franklin Templeton、Barings、Fidelity及Janus Henderson等業者均推出或擴充聚焦較高評等CLO分券的產品。

吸引力來自對浮動利率企業貸款的優先順位債權，尤其在政策利率仍高之際。投資級CLO分券在損失吸收順位上高於股權及較低評等的夾層分券，投資人得以收取較高收益，並由次順位資本先行吸收違約損失。不過，這種保障是結構性的，並非絕對安全：高利率持續提高標的貸款的利息收入，同時也在削弱槓桿最高借款人的資產負債表。

這項矛盾解釋了資金為何集中流入最高評等分券，即使BBB級基金近期也開始受到關注。Pimco警告信用損失循環已經展開，預測槓桿融資與私募直接放款的損失將明顯上升。投資長Dan Ivascyn也把複雜信用結構的擴張與全球金融危機前的累積情況相比，尤其是人工智慧基礎設施的資本需求，可能正助長過度寬鬆的評等或槓桿。

面向散戶的私募信貸工具則承受資產配置轉變的另一面。由於估值疑慮，以及軟體業借款人面臨人工智慧顛覆風險，投資人在第一季對私募信貸基金提出約$200億贖回要求。公開交易的CLO ETF可提供每日流動性與分散效果，企業發展公司及私募基金的投資人則可能必須認列折價，或等待贖回。

新發行CLO規模約達$580億，低於2025年同期的約$890億。ETF若持續吸金，可能支持下半年發行回升，但其作用是增加對資本結構優先部分的需求，而非消除較弱貸款借款人的財務惡化。

印尼的流動性壓力更為迫切。市場狀況惡化之際，兩檔持有當地債券的基金延後贖回。印尼央行也加強管控銀行外匯交易，確保交易與商業活動相關，而非用於投機。此前央行已在例會外升息以捍衛印尼盾；這些措施顯示，較高政策利率與全球油價下跌仍不足以恢復市場正常運作。

雅加達正尋求一項較長期的融資替代方案，規劃發行可能成為印尼首檔市政債的工具。雅加達與亞洲開發銀行及世界銀行合作，考慮在1年內發債，但省長Pramono Anung Wibowo並未說明金額。中央政府對雅加達的移轉款被削減約15兆印尼盾，相當於原始預算的16%，使這項計畫更為迫切。

雅加達也考慮設立財富基金，用於基礎設施與公共服務融資。財政部長Purbaya Yudhi Sadewa已口頭支持兩項計畫，但正式書面核准仍未取得。這筆交易將創設新的地方政府信用工具，其可行性取決於法規、償債收入來源及最終授權，而非只取決於省長提出的時程。

## 新興市場依國內通膨與財政條件分化

油價回落減輕了新興市場共同面臨的外部壓力，但國內通膨、財政政策及制度公信力使各國利率路徑顯著分歧。印度通膨低於預期，卻同時面臨預算可能偏離目標；巴西通膨超過目標區間上緣；波蘭更接近考慮降息，印尼則仍把重點放在捍衛匯率及市場流動性。

印度5月消費者物價年增率由4月的3.48%升至3.93%，低於4.02%的預測中位數，也仍略低於印度央行4%的目標。數據公布後，10年期政府公債殖利率下降3個基點至6.89%。在等待能源衝擊及盧比走勢更明朗之際，這項結果支持印度央行維持利率不變。

通膨組成卻不如整體數字溫和。食品通膨由4.20%加速至4.78%；國營煉油商也已調高燃料價格，只是漲幅仍低於衝突爆發以來國際原油的升幅。印度央行最近把截至2027年3月會計年度的通膨預測由4.6%上調至5.1%。Elara Securities與Kotak Mahindra的經濟學家預期，10月起將累計升息50個基點。

財政政策另增一項債券利率風險。據熟悉討論的官員表示，印度當局準備容許預算赤字占GDP比重較2月設定的4.3%目標擴大最多0.5個百分點，至4.8%。印度進口逾80%的原油，戰爭推高燃料與肥料補貼成本，先前調降燃料稅也減少政府收入。

Kotak估計，財政赤字可能超出目標30至50個基點，並帶來3,500億盧比的新增借款，可能透過國庫券籌措。調降燃料消費稅使政府少收約1.23兆盧比，補貼與收入影響合計估計形成約3兆盧比的財政缺口。政府計畫於今年稍後重新評估前景，並正在研究削減各部會支出。

財政消息出現時，印度公債曾短暫回吐漲幅，10年期殖利率升至6.91%，之後回到6.88%。這段走勢區分出兩項當前發展：整體通膨較溫和，支持利率不變；潛在新增借款則限制了政府公債的受益程度。

巴西的通膨意外方向正好相反。5月消費者物價較4月上漲0.58%，高於0.53%的預估，年增率因而升至4.72%，超過央行3%目標上下1.5個百分點容忍區間的上緣。食品與飲料價格上漲1.33%，住房成本也上升；政府增加燃料補貼後，交通價格則下跌。

漲價範圍廣泛，使巴西央行會議更難決策。Selic利率已降至14.5%，但基礎指標顯示，物價壓力正擴散到並非直接受到戰爭影響的類別。選舉前的財政支持同時支撐消費需求。Capital Economics預期下次決策將暫停降息，之後全年採取走走停停的寬鬆步調。

波蘭數據則較偏鴿派。5月通膨意外放緩至3.1%，降低中東衝擊把物價推升至央行容忍區間以外的疑慮。貨幣政策委員Ireneusz Dabrowski表示，現在降息的可能性高於升息，但他仍認為2026年小幅降息一次的機率非常低。

波蘭基準利率目前為3.75%。Dabrowski表示，10人委員會中的多數成員對通膨已轉趨樂觀，經濟成長放緩也降低收緊政策的必要性。他的說法與央行總裁Adam Glapinski及委員Gabriela Maslowska一致，使波蘭有別於歐洲央行與捷克，儘管各方都面對相同的全球能源干擾。

中國當局處理的是另一種失衡。貸款需求疲弱造成銀行體系流動性過剩，貨幣市場利率異常偏低。官員要求大型國有銀行減少對其他銀行放款，以提高銀行間融資成本，並抑制寬鬆流動性催生政府公債泡沫或加速資本外流的風險。這項干預針對流動性的價格與分配，而非正式調整政策利率。

各市場的分歧顯示，新興市場不會因油價下跌而採取一致反應。能源進口依賴固然重要，但其影響仍受到財政空間、國內通膨廣度、匯率壓力及央行公信力調節。印度獲得近期通膨緩解，卻面臨新增借款風險；巴西通膨壓縮降息空間；波蘭有更多餘裕等待，並可能轉向寬鬆；印尼與中國則運用行政及流動性工具，處理單靠利率水準無法解決的壓力。

## 日本預期升息，買方基礎仍顯脆弱

日本進入6月15日至16日央行會議之際，升息25個基點至約1%已幾乎完全反映在市場定價中，但JGB與日圓市場仍質疑央行行動是否夠快。總裁植田和男住院使政策溝通更為複雜，卻未明顯改變主流利率預測。

幾乎所有受訪的日本央行觀察人士都預期升息。這將使基準利率升至1995年以來最高，也是去年12月後首次升息。植田預定以書面提交意見，但不會參與投票；副總裁內田真一則將主持會後記者會。一般而言，政策聲明約於東京時間中午公布，記者會則在15:30舉行。

決策必須在內需疲弱與日圓及進口能源造成的通膨壓力之間取得平衡。政府補貼使公布的通膨低於日本央行2%目標，但央行預期能源成本將在本會計年度稍後推高物價。植田曾表示，消費者物價漲幅可能超過3%。10年期損益兩平通膨率5月升至2.35%的歷史新高，目前仍接近該水準。

儘管日本進行創紀錄的匯率干預，央行也逐步收緊政策，日圓仍徘徊在1美元兌160日圓附近。截至6月9日當週，槓桿基金把日圓空頭部位增至逾115,000口，為2017年11月以來最大。投資人在4月及5月干預後迅速重建空頭，把官方推動的日圓升值視為重新建立利差交易的機會。

若日本央行升息幅度超過預期，或暗示之後將更快收緊政策，這種部位結構可能引發非線性反應。2024年曾出現類似情況：升息與縮減購債同時發生，迫使利差交易迅速平倉。不過，這次投資人普遍預期升息及可能的匯率支持，除非指引出現重大改變，意外程度將較低。

政府公債買方基礎才是更具結構性的弱點。4月數據顯示，海外投資人賣出的超長天期JGB多於買進，為2024年以來首次。T. Rowe Price、Schroders及Brandywine Global等業者均縮減長天期曝險，或僅進行戰術性殖利率曲線交易。即使30年期殖利率在和平消息公布後下跌，年初至今仍上升逾30個基點。

對美元投資人而言，匯率避險後的30年期JGB殖利率超過6%，比同天期美國公債高約170個基點。這項表面上的價值仍不足以抵銷投資人對流動性不足、財政擴張、日本央行需求減少，以及政治力量要求放寬政策的疑慮。海外資產管理公司與日本國內保險業者仍不願成為超長債供給的穩定買家。

市場也有零星需求。近期債券交易績效在日本區域銀行中最佳的Iyogin Holdings，4月開始小量買進超長天期JGB，為10年來首次進行這類投資。執行長三好賢治預期，日本央行利率到2027年底將升至約1.5%，並認為可能出現幅度較大的50個基點升息。該行因預期殖利率還會上升，目前避開10年期債券，但會買進部分被認為估值具吸引力的超長債。

Iyogin重返市場值得注意，卻尚未解決整體市場的供給吸收問題。日本央行正以每季¥2,000億的速度縮減購債，計畫持續至2027年3月，但目前仍持有約半數流通政府債務。隨市場運作改善，官員預料將討論放慢或暫停進一步減購。放緩退場可以穩定殖利率，但溝通時必須避免讓市場認為貨幣政策服從於政府的財政偏好。

## 後續市場意義

第一項考驗，是美國與伊朗在收盤後宣布的進展能否成為實際執行的協議。夏立夫稱雙方將立即且永久停止軍事行動、美國將解除海上封鎖，並於6月19日在瑞士正式簽署。較早的報導把潛在安排描述為臨時備忘錄，並指出伊朗遭凍結資金、重建、核材料及美國軍事活動等問題仍未解決。

對利率而言，船舶能否實際通過荷莫茲海峽、各方是否持續遵守停火，以及石油運輸能否維持，均比再次宣稱協議即將達成更重要。海峽重開可減弱未來能源衝擊，但歐洲央行官員強調，產能受損、供應鏈改變與運輸風險溢價，仍可能使價格維持在戰前水準之上。若協議破裂，週五原油下跌所消除的通膨溢價將重新出現。

美國經濟活動數據於6月15日登場，美東時間08:30公布紐約州製造業調查，09:15公布5月工業生產。前次紐約州指數為19.6，4月工業生產則成長0.7%。若產出維持韌性，將支持經濟可以承受較高利率的觀點；若數據疲弱，即使通膨仍高於目標，也會強化暫緩行動的理由。

美國財政部將於6月15日美東時間11:30標售$890億13週期國庫券及$770億26週期國庫券，兩者均於6月18日交割。合計$1,660億的供給時點接近企業納稅日，將考驗貨幣市場需求；不過，標售結果仍須與票息債殖利率曲線及本週各央行決策分開評估。

6月16日將迎來日本央行決策及澳洲央行會議。市場預期日本央行把隔夜利率上調25個基點至約1%。植田缺席之際，內田如何說明後續升息與購債安排將是焦點。若指引暗示下一次升息可能較快到來，將衝擊擁擠的日圓空頭及疲弱的超長天期JGB需求；若訊號審慎，市場對央行落後於通膨與匯率變化的疑慮可能加深。

澳洲央行在2026年已升息3次，市場預期本次把現金利率目標維持在4.35%。自5月5日會議以來，澳洲10年期殖利率已下跌約20個基點，因就業、消費者信心及企業調查疲弱，使投資人判斷升息循環接近尾聲。交換市場反映年底前再升息一次的機率約為50%，低於5月會後立即反映的再升息兩次。總裁Michele Bullock如何看待第二輪通膨風險，將決定這波債市漲勢能否延續。

中國將於6月16日上海時間10:00公布5月工業生產、零售銷售、固定資產投資及失業率。工業生產年增率預期由4.1%升至4.2%；零售銷售在前月成長0.2%後，預測本月持平；年初至今固定資產投資預期在前次下降1.6%後進一步萎縮2%；失業率則預估維持5.2%。在官員試圖防止銀行間流動性過剩之際，這組數據將檢驗內需疲弱是否足以支持更寬鬆政策。

同日美東時間08:30，美國將公布進出口物價、房屋開工及建築許可。4月進口物價上漲2%，出口物價上漲3.5%，因此5月數據可直接檢驗外部物價傳導。前次房屋開工年率為146.5萬戶，建築許可初值為142.3萬戶，兩者也提供對利率敏感需求的平行觀察。

美國財政部6月16日的操作將由短期國庫券延伸至長天期債券。美東時間11:30預定標售$650億6週期國庫券；13:00將增額發行$130億、票面利率5%、剩餘天期19年11個月的公債，6月22日交割，2046年5月15日到期。13:40至14:00另有流動性支持型買回，最多可收購$40億7年至10年期非指標名目票息債。增額發行將直接反映波動較大天期的需求，買回則處理市場流動性的另一環節。

美國5月零售銷售將於6月17日美東時間08:30公布，是聯準會決策前最後一項重要消費數據。經濟學家預期月增0.4%，前值為0.5%。若再度穩健成長，將強化密西根消費者信心改善所呈現的訊號，使聯準會更難忽視需求具韌性與通膨偏高的交互作用；若結果疲弱，則會擴大目前在歐洲與澳洲較為明顯的成長疑慮。

FOMC將於美東時間14:00公布利率決策及經濟預測摘要，Warsh於14:30主持就任後首次會後記者會。市場普遍預期利率維持在3.50%-3.75%。真正影響市場的訊息，是官員會否刪除寬鬆傾向、有多少份利率預測顯示2026年升息，以及Warsh能否把控制通膨呈現為委員會的首要風險，同時避免讓市場認為政策已預先承諾。

英國6月17日美東時間02:00公布CPI，預期年增率由2.8%升至3%。數據公布後，英國央行將於6月18日決策，市場預期利率維持在3.75%。投票分布及政策指引必須同時回應4月GDP萎縮，以及家庭對未來1年通膨預期達4%、5年期預期達3.9%的情況。即使不升息，持續出售英國公債仍會形成緊縮效果。

美國財政部將於6月18日增額發行$240億5年期抗通膨債券。該批TIPS票面利率為1.25%，剩餘天期4年10個月，6月30日交割，2031年4月15日到期。標售安排在聯準會決策後，可檢驗市場對實質殖利率的需求；6月12日名目殖利率的變動幾乎全由損益兩平通膨率上升所致，而非實質利率走高。

6月19日六月節假期，美國固定收益市場建議全天休市。投資人因而必須在更短時間內消化聯準會、英國央行、美國數據、財政部供給及任何正式伊朗協議。事件集中使落實細節與標售表現更重要：下一波持久的利率走勢不能只靠油價下跌的預期，而取決於通膨數據、央行指引及實際能源流量能否確認衝擊確實正在消退。

overall_summary.headline: 油價壓力緩解仍未消除聯準會溢價，美債殖利率上升

美國公債收盤小幅走弱，回吐前一交易日部分漲幅，但全週仍保有漲勢。2年期殖利率上升1.9個基點至4.082%，5年期上升2.2個基點至4.207%，10年期上升1.9個基點至4.481%，30年期則小升1.2個基點至4.968%。10年期實質殖利率幾乎持平於2.151%，損益兩平通膨率則上升2個基點至2.33%，顯示現貨原油下跌未能再度壓低長期通膨補償。

美國與伊朗朝就荷莫茲海峽達成協議更進一步，WTI下跌3.23%至$84.88，布蘭特原油下跌3.37%至$87.33。歐洲短端公債強勁上漲，但投資人衡量已實現的通膨壓力、美國經濟活動的韌性，以及聯準會再次升息的可觀機率後，美國公債早盤漲勢消退。密西根大學消費者信心升至48.9，通膨預期下降，但1年期讀數仍高達4.6%。

long_thesis.english_markdown:
## Opening Fixed-Income Thesis

Treasuries ended June 12 modestly cheaper even as another decline in oil reduced the immediate inflation threat from the Iran war. The 2-year yield rose 1.9 basis points to 4.082%, the 5-year increased 2.2 basis points to 4.207%, the 10-year added 1.9 basis points to 4.481% and the 30-year edged 1.2 basis points higher to 4.968%. The move partly reversed the previous session’s rally but left yields lower over the week, including declines of 6.6 basis points at 2 years and 5 basis points at 10 years.

The session’s defining feature was the Treasury market’s reluctance to extend an early global-duration rally on diplomatic optimism alone. WTI fell 3.23% to $84.88 and Brent declined 3.37% to $87.33 as the US and Iran moved closer to an agreement over the Strait of Hormuz. European front ends rallied sharply, with 2-year UK yields falling 14 basis points to 4.20% and German equivalents dropping nearly 10 basis points to 2.58%. Treasuries initially participated, but the US move faded as investors retained substantial odds of another Federal Reserve increase and approached Kevin Warsh’s first meeting as chair.

The composition of the US close showed where the resistance came from. The 10-year real yield was almost unchanged, slipping 0.1 basis point to 2.151%, while the 10-year breakeven rose 2 basis points to 2.33%. Lower spot crude therefore did not produce another decline in longer-run inflation compensation. The 2s10s curve was unchanged at 39.9 basis points, and 2s30s flattened only 0.7 basis point to 88.6 basis points. The nearly parallel rise in coupon yields conveyed continued policy caution rather than a fresh long-end fiscal or term-premium shock.

US consumer data gave the Fed some relief but not an all-clear. Preliminary University of Michigan sentiment rose to 48.9 in June from 44.8, while one-year inflation expectations eased to 4.6% from 4.8% and the long-run measure fell to 3.4% from 3.9%. The improvement was broad across current conditions and expectations, but the inflation readings remained elevated in absolute terms. A separate survey of economists pushed the median forecast for the first Fed cut into June 2027, while market pricing continued to assign a large probability to a rate increase before the end of 2026.

Risk assets welcomed the decline in energy prices and the prospect of a diplomatic settlement. The S&P 500 gained 0.50%, the Nasdaq 100 rose 0.64% and the PHLX Semiconductor Index advanced 1.52%, while the VIX fell 9.05% to 17.68. SpaceX’s record $75 billion initial public offering opened 11% above its $135 offer price and finished its debut 19% higher, reinforcing an equity backdrop of resilient demand for technology and artificial-intelligence exposure. The dollar index eased 0.11%.

The cross-asset signal was not uniformly complacent. Gold climbed 3.05% to $4,215, investment-grade bond-fund prices slipped slightly and high-yield funds were essentially unchanged. The combination suggested that investors were willing to reduce the most immediate energy and volatility premium without treating the geopolitical or inflation outlook as settled.

That distinction became more important after the 17:00 ET fixed-income cutoff. Pakistan Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif said the US and Iran had agreed to an immediate and permanent cessation of military operations and that a formal signing was scheduled for June 19 in Switzerland. President Donald Trump was also said to be preparing to remove the US naval blockade. The announcement materially advanced the diplomatic story, but it occurred after the completed bond close and could not have caused Friday’s yield move. Implementation of the ceasefire, actual reopening of Hormuz and the durability of the terms remained the next tests.

## Oil Relief Meets a Persistent Fed Premium

The early Treasury bid followed a renewed turn toward diplomacy. Trump said a deal was close after previously threatening additional military action, while officials described negotiations over an interim arrangement to reopen the Strait of Hormuz. Brent fell below $86 during European trading for the first time in 3 months. At that stage, the US 2-year yield was reported about 2 basis points lower near 4.05%, compared with its eventual daily-history reading of 4.082%.

The reversal by the completed close showed that the rates market was distinguishing between a lower prospective energy impulse and the inflation already embedded in prices and policy expectations. The previous day’s producer-price report had shown a broad increase in pipeline costs, while May consumer inflation had reached 4.2% from a year earlier. Friday’s cheaper crude improved the outlook for future headline inflation, but it did not undo those realized increases or settle how much businesses would pass through to consumers.

The Michigan survey added a more favorable current signal. Headline sentiment increased by 4.1 points to 48.9. Current conditions rose to 48.4 from 45.8 and expectations improved to 49.3 from 44.1, with early-month gasoline relief supporting views of personal finances and business conditions. The one-year inflation expectation declined 0.2 percentage point, and the 0.5-point fall in the long-run measure was larger.

Those declines matter for the Fed because household expectations can influence wage demands and price-setting behavior. They were not low enough to establish that the energy shock had disappeared from consumer psychology. A 4.6% one-year reading remained well above the Fed’s objective, while the improvement in sentiment reduced the case for interpreting high inflation as coinciding with an abrupt collapse in demand.

Employer compensation data supplied another labor-cost observation without resolving the policy debate. Civilian compensation averaged $49.32 per hour in March, consisting of $33.72 in wages and salaries and $15.60 in benefits. That compared with $48.78, $33.45 and $15.33, respectively, in December. Private-industry compensation averaged $46.60, including $32.60 in wages and $14.01 in benefits, up from total compensation of $46.15 in December. The figures describe compensation levels rather than the growth rate measured by the Employment Cost Index, but they show that both wage and benefit costs remained substantial for employers.

The competing signals leave the June 16-17 FOMC meeting focused less on the widely expected decision than on the bias around the next move. A survey of 35 economists showed a median expectation for cuts in June and December 2027, taking the target range to 3%-3.25%. In the preceding March survey, respondents had expected the same destination to be reached through reductions during 2026. Only three economists forecast a rate increase this year, in contrast with futures pricing that continued to lean toward tightening.

There was much greater agreement on the immediate meeting. Both economists and investors overwhelmingly expected the Fed to hold the target at 3.50%-3.75%, and 71% of surveyed economists anticipated a unanimous vote. The more consequential question was whether officials would retain language that made a cut appear more likely than an increase. Three-quarters of respondents expected the FOMC either to remove that easing bias or replace it with wording that treated the next adjustment as equally likely in either direction.

The distribution of perceived risks had changed sharply. Eighty-two percent of surveyed economists said inflation was a greater danger than unemployment, and none identified the labor market as the larger risk. In December, more than half had placed greater weight on employment. That shift helps explain why lower crude and softer household inflation expectations produced only a temporary rally: the burden has moved to incoming data to show that the broadening price pressure has stopped.

Market participants were more hawkish than the economist median. Muhammad Qubbaj, co-head of US interest-rate products at Goldman Sachs, said resilient activity, higher prices and the corporate artificial-intelligence spending boom justified current rate pricing. Traders assigned roughly a 75% probability to an increase by year-end and fully priced a move by March 2027. The first meeting under Warsh was viewed as a test of whether he would emphasize inflation control while building consensus inside a divided committee.

The completed curve did not signal a major escalation in that tightening view. The 2-year and 10-year yields rose by the same 1.9 basis points, and the 30-year increased less. Yet the failure to sustain an oil-led rally showed that the market no longer regarded every diplomatic headline as sufficient to remove policy premium. A ceasefire can reduce the next inflation impulse; it cannot by itself determine whether the current funds rate is restrictive enough for an economy that is still generating firm employment, consumer spending and capital investment.

Treasury cash activity also moderated after the previous session’s geopolitical rally. FINRA recorded $893 billion of par activity across 340,363 trades, 24.8% less than on June 11. Nominal-coupon activity fell 20.8% to $734.1 billion, while activity in maturities above 20 years declined 39.6%. The turnover figures do not identify investor direction, but they show that the modest selloff occurred during a quieter session rather than another exceptionally active repricing.

## Europe’s Front End Rallies Into a Harder Policy Debate

European government bonds responded more forcefully than Treasuries to the fall in oil because the energy shock had become the immediate organizing principle for both the European Central Bank and the Bank of England. The short end led the move, with UK 2-year yields down 14 basis points and German 2-year yields almost 10 basis points lower. Traders reduced expectations for repeated tightening after the ECB’s quarter-point increase, while UK pricing moved toward only one increase by November.

The rally did not amount to a rejection of the ECB’s decision. Officials had raised the deposit rate to 2.25% after euro-area inflation reached 3.2% in May and underlying pressure strengthened. The new information on Friday was that lower oil could limit the need for a rapid sequence, even as policymakers continued to warn that the shock had already spread beyond energy.

Bundesbank President Joachim Nagel said the ECB was prepared to raise rates again in July if necessary. He argued that high energy costs were affecting other prices and core inflation, making the June move necessary even if the geopolitical situation improved quickly. The International Monetary Fund likewise assumed 50 basis points of cumulative tightening during 2026 because of the risk that both headline and core inflation would remain above 2% into 2028.

Peter Kazimir, Slovakia’s central-bank governor, went further in arguing that policy would need to rise again. He said price pressure would not return to target immediately even under a peace agreement, because damaged production capacity and wider inflation transmission could persist. The June core-inflation reading may be decisive for the timing, although he said there was no agreement on a July move and noted that September would bring another set of forecasts.

France’s Emmanuel Moulin identified a more specific boundary in the transmission. Oil and gas increases had begun to pass through to other goods and services, including parts of the services basket, but he had not yet seen second-round effects through wages. Moulin did not endorse a predetermined rate path. His distinction left the ECB with a reason to act against broadening prices without assuming that the most persistent wage-price mechanism was already established.

Slovenian central-bank chief Primoz Dolenc offered a more cautious policy signal. He said the June hike was necessary after hard data showed higher inflation and weaker growth, but described the move as sufficient for the moment and gave no indication about the next decision. Even a quick reopening of Hormuz, in his assessment, would not make crude immediately available throughout the supply chain.

The dispute therefore concerns pace rather than whether the energy shock matters. Nagel and Kazimir emphasized persistence and the need to preserve the option of another increase. Dolenc and Moulin stressed meeting-by-meeting judgment and the absence of some second-round effects. Markets reduced the extent of expected tightening as oil fell, while still pricing at least one more ECB increase and a meaningful chance of another by the first half of 2027.

Growth risk makes that path harder to sustain. UK gross domestic product contracted 0.1% in April after expanding 0.3% in March, the first monthly decline since August 2025. Services fell 0.2%, production was unchanged and construction increased 0.1%. The broader trend was firmer: output grew 0.7% in the 3 months through April, compared with 0.6% in the 3 months through March. The monthly decline weakened the near-term picture without establishing that the earlier expansion had fully reversed.

UK household inflation expectations moved in the opposite direction. The median expectation for the coming year rose to 4.0% from 3.2% in February. Expectations for the following 12 months increased to 3.5% from 3.2%, while the 5-year measure reached 3.9% from 3.7%. Perceived current inflation climbed to 5.0% from 4.6%.

The interest-rate responses were equally striking: 53% of households expected rates to rise during the next year, up from 30% in February, while 23% expected no change and 11% anticipated a decline. That combination of weaker monthly output and higher inflation expectations captures the Bank of England’s dilemma ahead of its June 18 meeting. Lower oil improves the forward picture, but the household survey indicates that the preceding shock has already altered expectations.

Governor Andrew Bailey added a balance-sheet dimension over the weekend by defending active gilt sales. He said quantitative easing and its reversal had been broadly neutral for taxpayers over the full period, noting that the government had transferred about £108 billion to the Bank since late 2022 after receiving almost £124 billion in earlier profits. Bailey rejected calls to pause sales, arguing that a smaller balance sheet would restore room to buy assets in a future shock. Continued active sales tighten financial conditions even if the Monetary Policy Committee leaves Bank Rate at 3.75%.

## Credit Demand Favors Shorter Risk and Senior Claims

The decline in oil improved the broad tone in European credit, where investors unwound some wartime hedges, but new financing showed that demand remained selective. Borrowers offering shorter maturities, seniority or a clear yield premium found capacity. Structures exposed to lower-quality borrowers or uncertain liquidity continued to receive closer scrutiny.

Lloyds Banking Group sold ¥75 billion, or about $468 million, of yen-denominated Samurai bonds, its first such offering in 2 years. The deal came as foreign issuance in Japan reached ¥503 billion in the fiscal year through June 12, the highest for the period since 2015, when sales reached ¥538 billion.

Japanese investors have favored Samurai bonds because their maturities are often shorter and their spreads wider than comparable domestic debt, an attractive combination while Japanese policy rates are rising. Yen funding can also remain competitive for foreign issuers after currency-swap costs because benchmark Japanese yields are still below those in the US and Europe.

One Lloyds tranche consisted of 6-year bonds callable after 5 years at 78 basis points over swaps. Sumitomo Mitsui Banking Corp., rated only one notch higher by S&P, had sold 2031 notes in April at 28 basis points over swaps. The 50-basis-point difference gave Japanese buyers visible compensation for the foreign bank exposure while allowing Lloyds to tap a deep domestic savings pool.

A larger structural shift was visible in collateralized-loan-obligation funds. Inflows into US CLO exchange-traded funds exceeded $9 billion during 2026, up from almost $7 billion during the comparable period a year earlier. Roughly $740 million entered during the first week of June, the largest weekly inflow since early February. Franklin Templeton, Barings, Fidelity and Janus Henderson were among the firms introducing or expanding products focused on higher-rated CLO tranches.

The attraction lies in senior claims on floating-rate corporate loans at a time when policy rates remain high. Investment-grade CLO tranches sit above equity and lower-rated mezzanine pieces in the loss waterfall, allowing investors to collect elevated income while junior capital absorbs the first defaults. The protection is structural rather than absolute: persistent high rates are strengthening the income on the underlying loans while simultaneously weakening the balance sheets of the most leveraged borrowers.

That tension explains why the inflows have concentrated in the highest-rated tranches, even though BBB funds have recently gained interest. Pimco warned that the credit-loss cycle had begun and forecast materially higher losses in leveraged finance and private direct lending. Chief Investment Officer Dan Ivascyn also compared the expansion of complex credit structures with the buildup before the global financial crisis, particularly where capital needs for artificial-intelligence infrastructure may be encouraging generous ratings or leverage.

Retail private-credit vehicles have experienced the other side of the allocation change. Investors requested about $20 billion of withdrawals from private-credit funds in Q1 amid valuation concerns and the exposure of software borrowers to artificial-intelligence disruption. Public CLO ETFs offer daily liquidity and diversification, while business development companies and private funds can force investors to recognize discounts or wait for redemptions.

New CLO issuance had reached about $58 billion, down from roughly $89 billion at the same point of 2025. Continued ETF inflows could support a second-half recovery in issuance, but they would do so by increasing demand for the senior parts of the capital structure, not by eliminating the deterioration among weaker loan borrowers.

Liquidity pressure was more immediate in Indonesia, where two funds holding local bonds delayed redemptions as market conditions deteriorated. Bank Indonesia also tightened control over banks’ foreign-exchange dealings to ensure transactions were linked to commercial activity rather than speculation. Those steps followed an off-cycle rate increase designed to defend the rupiah and showed that higher policy rates and lower global oil were not sufficient to restore normal market functioning.

Jakarta is pursuing a longer-term funding alternative through what would be Indonesia’s first municipal bond. The city is working with the Asian Development Bank and World Bank on a possible issue within a year, although Governor Pramono Anung Wibowo did not specify an amount. The plan gained urgency after transfers to Jakarta were cut by about 15 trillion rupiah, or 16% of its initial budget.

The city is also considering a wealth fund to finance infrastructure and public services. Finance Minister Purbaya Yudhi Sadewa had verbally endorsed both initiatives, but formal written approval remained outstanding. The transaction would create a new local-government credit instrument; its feasibility depends on regulation, revenue backing and final authorization rather than the governor’s timetable alone.

## Emerging Markets Split Along Domestic Inflation and Fiscal Lines

The retreat in oil eased a common external pressure on emerging markets, but domestic inflation, fiscal policy and institutional credibility produced sharply different rate paths. India combined softer-than-expected inflation with the prospect of budget slippage. Brazil’s inflation exceeded the top of its target range. Poland moved closer to considering a cut, while Indonesia remained focused on currency defense and market liquidity.

India’s consumer-price inflation increased to 3.93% in May from 3.48% in April, below the 4.02% median estimate and still just under the Reserve Bank of India’s 4% target. The 10-year government yield was down 3 basis points at 6.89% after the release. The result supported the RBI’s decision to hold rates while waiting for more clarity on the energy shock and the rupee.

The composition was less benign than the headline surprise. Food inflation accelerated to 4.78% from 4.20%, and state-owned refiners had already raised fuel prices, though by less than the increase in international crude since the conflict began. The RBI recently lifted its inflation projection for the fiscal year through March 2027 to 5.1% from 4.6%. Economists at Elara Securities and Kotak Mahindra expected a cumulative 50 basis points of increases beginning in October.

Fiscal policy added a separate source of duration risk. Indian authorities were prepared to allow the budget deficit to widen by as much as 0.5 percentage point to 4.8% of gross domestic product, compared with the 4.3% target set in February, according to an official familiar with the discussions. India imports more than 80% of its crude, and the war increased fuel and fertilizer subsidy costs while earlier fuel-tax reductions lowered revenue.

Kotak estimated fiscal slippage of 30 to 50 basis points and potential incremental borrowing of 350 billion rupees, likely through Treasury bills. The reduction in fuel excise duties had cost about 1.23 trillion rupees, while combined subsidy and revenue effects were estimated to have created a fiscal hole of roughly 3 trillion rupees. The government planned to reassess the outlook later in the year and was examining spending cuts across ministries.

Indian bonds briefly surrendered gains when the fiscal report appeared, with the 10-year yield reaching 6.91% before returning to 6.88%. The sequence separated two current developments: softer headline inflation supported the rate hold, while the possibility of additional borrowing limited the benefit for sovereign bonds.

Brazil faced the opposite inflation surprise. Consumer prices rose 0.58% in May from April, above the 0.53% estimate, lifting annual inflation to 4.72%. That exceeded the upper edge of the central bank’s 3% target plus-or-minus 1.5-percentage-point tolerance range. Food and beverages increased 1.33%, while housing costs also rose. Transportation prices declined after the government introduced additional fuel subsidies.

The breadth of the increase complicates the Banco Central do Brasil’s meeting. The Selic rate had already been reduced to 14.5%, but underlying measures suggested that pressure was extending beyond categories directly affected by the war. Fiscal support ahead of the election was sustaining consumer demand at the same time. Capital Economics expected a pause at the next decision and a stop-start easing cycle during the remainder of the year.

Poland’s evidence pointed in a more dovish direction. May inflation slowed unexpectedly to 3.1%, reducing concern that the Middle East shock would push prices beyond the central bank’s tolerance range. Monetary Policy Council member Ireneusz Dabrowski said a cut was now more likely than an increase, although he described the chance of one modest reduction during 2026 as very small.

The Polish benchmark stands at 3.75%. Dabrowski said most of the 10-member council had become more optimistic about inflation, while slower economic growth also reduced the need to tighten. His comments aligned with Governor Adam Glapinski and council member Gabriela Maslowska, distinguishing Poland from the ECB and the Czech Republic even though all faced the same global energy disturbance.

China’s authorities addressed a different distortion. Weak loan demand had produced excess banking-system liquidity and unusually low money-market rates. Officials told large state-owned banks to reduce lending to other banks, an effort to lift interbank borrowing costs and limit the risk that easy liquidity would encourage a government-bond bubble or accelerate capital outflows. The intervention was aimed at the price and distribution of liquidity rather than a formal change in the policy rate.

The dispersion across these markets argues against a single emerging-market response to cheaper oil. Energy import dependence matters, but it is being filtered through fiscal capacity, domestic inflation breadth, currency pressure and central-bank credibility. India received near-term inflation relief but confronted additional borrowing risk; Brazil’s inflation narrowed the space for cuts; Poland gained room to wait and possibly ease; Indonesia and China used administrative and liquidity tools to address stresses that rate levels alone had not resolved.

## Japan’s Expected Hike Confronts a Fragile Buyer Base

Japan entered the June 15-16 Bank of Japan meeting with a quarter-point increase to about 1% almost fully expected, yet the JGB and yen markets continued to question whether the central bank was moving quickly enough. Governor Kazuo Ueda’s hospitalization added a communication complication without materially changing the prevailing rate forecast.

Almost all surveyed BOJ watchers expected the increase, which would lift the benchmark to its highest level since 1995 and mark the first hike since December. Ueda was due to submit his views in writing but would not vote. Deputy Governor Shinichi Uchida was scheduled to conduct the post-meeting press conference, normally held at 15:30 in Tokyo after the policy statement around noon.

The decision must balance weak domestic demand against inflation pressure from the yen and imported energy. Government subsidies had held measured inflation below the BOJ’s 2% target, but the bank expected energy costs to lift prices later in the fiscal year. Ueda had indicated that consumer inflation could exceed 3%. The 10-year breakeven reached a record 2.35% in May and remained near that level.

The yen was hovering around 160 per dollar despite record intervention and the BOJ’s gradual tightening. Leveraged funds increased bearish yen positions to more than 115,000 contracts in the week through June 9, the largest short position since November 2017. Investors had rebuilt those positions quickly after intervention in April and May, treating official yen strength as an opportunity to re-establish carry trades.

The positioning raises the risk of a nonlinear response if the BOJ delivers more than the expected increase or signals faster subsequent tightening. A similar combination of a rate rise and reduced bond purchases forced a rapid carry unwind in 2024. This time, however, investors broadly expect both a hike and possible currency support, reducing the element of surprise unless the guidance changes materially.

The government-bond buyer base remains the more structural vulnerability. April data showed overseas investors selling more super-long JGBs than they bought for the first time since 2024. T. Rowe Price, Schroders and Brandywine Global were among firms that reduced long-duration exposure or confined activity to tactical curve positions. The 30-year yield remained more than 30 basis points higher for the year even after falling on the peace announcement.

For dollar-based investors, currency-hedged 30-year JGB yields exceeded 6%, about 170 basis points more than comparable Treasuries. That apparent value had not overcome concern about illiquidity, fiscal expansion, reduced BOJ demand and political pressure for easier policy. Foreign managers and domestic insurers remained reluctant to become dependable buyers of super-long supply.

There were pockets of demand. Iyogin Holdings, the Japanese regional bank with the strongest recent bond-trading record, began making small purchases of super-long JGBs in April, its first investment purchases in the market in a decade. Chief Executive Kenji Miyoshi expected the BOJ rate to reach about 1.5% by the end of 2027 and saw a possibility of larger 50-basis-point moves. The bank was avoiding 10-year bonds for now because it expected yields to rise further, while buying selected ultra-long issues it regarded as attractively valued.

Iyogin’s return is notable but does not yet solve the market’s absorption problem. The BOJ is reducing purchases by ¥200 billion per quarter through March 2027 and still owns roughly half of outstanding government debt. Officials were expected to discuss slowing or pausing further reductions as market functioning improved. A slower withdrawal could stabilize yields, but it would have to be communicated without suggesting that monetary policy was being subordinated to the government’s fiscal preferences.

## Forward Market Significance

The first test is whether the post-close US-Iran announcement becomes an operative settlement. Sharif described an immediate and permanent cessation of military activity, removal of the US naval blockade and a formal June 19 signing in Switzerland. Earlier accounts had described the prospective arrangement as an interim memorandum and identified unresolved questions involving frozen Iranian funds, reconstruction, nuclear material and US military activity.

Actual passage through Hormuz, continued adherence to the ceasefire and sustained oil shipments will matter more for rates than another statement that an agreement is near. Reopening the strait would reduce the prospective energy impulse, but ECB officials have emphasized that damaged capacity, altered supply chains and freight-risk premiums may keep prices above their prewar levels. A breakdown would restore the inflation premium that Friday’s crude decline removed.

US activity data begin June 15 with the Empire State manufacturing survey at 08:30 ET and May industrial production at 09:15. The previous Empire reading was 19.6, while production had increased 0.7% in April. Resilient output would support the view that the economy can absorb higher rates; weakness would strengthen the case for waiting even if inflation remains above target.

Treasury will sell $89 billion of 13-week bills and $77 billion of 26-week bills at 11:30 ET on June 15. Both issues settle June 18. The $166 billion combined offering arrives near the corporate tax date and will test money-market demand, though auction results must be assessed separately from the coupon curve and from the week’s central-bank decisions.

June 16 brings the Bank of Japan decision and the Reserve Bank of Australia meeting. The BOJ is expected to raise the overnight rate by 25 basis points to about 1%. With Ueda absent, Uchida’s explanation of subsequent tightening and bond purchases will be central. Guidance suggesting that another increase could follow relatively quickly would challenge crowded yen shorts and weak demand for super-long JGBs. A cautious signal could intensify concern that the bank is behind inflation and the currency.

The RBA is expected to hold its cash-rate target at 4.35% after three increases in 2026. Australian 10-year yields have fallen about 20 basis points since the May 5 meeting as weak employment, consumer confidence and business surveys led investors to judge that the tightening cycle was near its end. Swaps assigned roughly a 50% chance to one more increase by year-end, down from pricing for two additional moves immediately after the May meeting. Governor Michele Bullock’s treatment of second-round inflation risk will determine whether that rally can extend.

China releases May industrial production, retail sales, fixed-asset investment and unemployment at 10:00 in Shanghai on June 16. Industrial production is expected to increase 4.2% from a year earlier after 4.1%, retail sales are forecast to be unchanged after a 0.2% gain, fixed-asset investment is expected to contract 2% year to date after a 1.6% decline and unemployment is seen holding at 5.2%. The package will test whether weak domestic demand justifies easier policy even as officials try to prevent excessive interbank liquidity.

US import and export prices, housing starts and building permits arrive at 08:30 ET the same day. April import prices had risen 2% and export prices 3.5%, making the May figures a direct check on external price transmission. Starts previously ran at a 1.465 million annualized pace and permits at a preliminary 1.423 million, providing a parallel measure of rate-sensitive demand.

Treasury’s June 16 operations extend from cash bills into duration. A $65 billion 6-week bill auction is scheduled for 11:30 ET. At 13:00, the government will reopen $13 billion of a 5% bond with 19 years and 11 months remaining, settling June 22 and maturing May 15, 2046. A liquidity-support buyback from 13:40 to 14:00 may accept as much as $4 billion of off-the-run nominal coupons in the 7- to 10-year sector. The reopening will give a direct demand reading in a volatile maturity, while the buyback addresses a different part of market liquidity.

May US retail sales at 08:30 ET on June 17 are the final major consumption input before the Fed decision. Economists expect a 0.4% monthly increase after 0.5% in April. Another firm gain would reinforce the evidence from improved Michigan sentiment and make it harder for the Fed to dismiss the interaction of resilient demand and elevated inflation. A weak result would broaden the growth concerns currently visible more clearly in Europe and Australia.

The FOMC announces its decision and Summary of Economic Projections at 14:00 ET, followed by Warsh’s first post-meeting press conference at 14:30. A hold at 3.50%-3.75% is widely expected. The market-moving information will be whether officials remove the easing bias, how many projections show an increase during 2026 and whether Warsh presents inflation control as the committee’s dominant risk without appearing to pre-commit.

UK CPI, released at 02:00 ET on June 17, is expected to rise 3% from a year earlier after 2.8%. The result precedes the Bank of England’s June 18 decision, for which a hold at 3.75% is expected. The vote split and guidance must reconcile the April GDP contraction with household inflation expectations of 4% over the coming year and 3.9% over 5 years. Continued gilt sales add restraint even without a rate increase.

Treasury will reopen $24 billion of 5-year inflation-protected securities on June 18. The 1.25% TIPS have 4 years and 10 months remaining, settle June 30 and mature April 15, 2031. The auction follows the Fed and will test demand for real yields after the June 12 nominal move came almost entirely from a rise in breakeven inflation rather than real rates.

Juneteenth brings a full recommended close for the US fixed-income market on June 19. The holiday compresses the period in which investors can respond to the Fed, the BOE, US data, Treasury supply and any formal Iran agreement. That concentration raises the importance of implementation details and auction execution: the next durable rates move will depend not on the promise of lower oil alone, but on whether inflation data, central-bank guidance and physical energy flows confirm that the shock is actually receding.

section_summaries.summary: Treasury yields rose modestly across the curve as an oil-led early rally faded, leaving the 2s10s curve unchanged and the 2s30s only slightly flatter. Lower crude reduced the prospective energy impulse, but higher breakeven inflation, elevated household inflation expectations and hawkish Fed pricing preserved the policy premium. section_summaries.section_title: Oil Relief Meets a Persistent Fed Premium
section_summaries.summary: Cheaper crude and improved Michigan readings offered the Fed some relief, but they did not erase broad pipeline inflation, May consumer inflation of 4.2% or substantial employer compensation costs. Economists overwhelmingly expected a June 16-17 hold at 3.50%-3.75%, while three-quarters anticipated a neutral or less dovish policy bias. Traders remained more hawkish, assigning roughly a 75% probability to an increase by year-end and fully pricing one by March 2027.

section_summaries.market_read: Lower oil softened the expected tightening path without reversing concern that energy costs had already spread beyond fuel.
section_summaries.section_title: Europe’s Front End Rallies Into a Harder Policy Debate
section_summaries.summary: UK and German 2-year yields fell sharply as cheaper oil reduced expectations for repeated tightening, but European policymakers continued to debate pace rather than the relevance of the inflation shock. Nagel and Kazimir emphasized broadening price pressure and the option of another ECB increase, while Moulin and Dolenc stressed meeting-by-meeting judgment and limited evidence of wage second-round effects. In the UK, weaker April GDP collided with rising household inflation expectations ahead of the June 18 BOE decision.

section_summaries.market_read: High policy rates support floating-rate income while simultaneously weakening the most leveraged borrowers.
section_summaries.next_check: Whether continued CLO ETF inflows revive H2 issuance without masking losses among weaker loan borrowers.
section_summaries.section_title: Credit Demand Favors Shorter Risk and Senior Claims
section_summaries.summary: Credit demand remained selective despite the improvement in risk tone. Lloyds attracted Japanese buyers with a shorter, wider-spread Samurai deal, while more than $9 billion of 2026 inflows into US CLO ETFs concentrated in senior tranches. Private-credit funds faced about $20 billion of Q1 withdrawal requests, Pimco warned that the leveraged-credit loss cycle had begun, and Indonesian bond funds delayed redemptions. Jakarta’s proposed municipal bond still requires regulation, revenue backing and formal approval.

section_summaries.market_read: Energy exposure was filtered through fiscal capacity, domestic inflation breadth, currency pressure and policy credibility.
section_summaries.section_title: Emerging Markets Split Along Domestic Inflation and Fiscal Lines
section_summaries.summary: Cheaper oil did not produce a common emerging-market rates outcome. India’s softer-than-expected 3.93% inflation supported the RBI’s hold, but possible deficit slippage and additional borrowing limited the bond rally. Brazil’s 4.72% inflation narrowed room for further cuts, while Poland’s unexpected slowdown to 3.1% made a modest cut more plausible. Indonesia remained focused on currency defense and liquidity, and China restricted interbank lending to curb excess liquidity without changing its policy rate.

section_summaries.market_read: An expected hike offers limited surprise unless the BOJ materially changes its guidance or purchase plans.
section_summaries.section_title: Japan’s Expected Hike Confronts a Fragile Buyer Base
section_summaries.summary: A 25-basis-point BOJ increase to about 1% was almost fully expected, leaving guidance and bond purchases as the larger market variables. Crowded yen shorts create unwind risk if subsequent tightening is faster than anticipated, but the structural concern is weak demand for super-long JGBs amid reduced BOJ buying, fiscal uncertainty and poor liquidity. Selective purchases by Iyogin have not yet solved the market’s broader absorption problem.

The next durable rates move depends on evidence that the energy shock is actually receding and on how central banks respond to persistent inflation. Hormuz flows and the planned June 19 signing will test the diplomatic advance; the BOJ’s June 16 guidance will confront crowded yen shorts and fragile JGB demand; and the June 17 FOMC projections and Warsh press conference will determine whether the Fed retains an easing bias. US activity data, Treasury supply and the BOE decision add further tests before the June 19 market close.

overall_summary.headline: Treasury yields rise as oil relief fails to dislodge the Fed premium
overall_summary.session_narrative:
Treasuries finished modestly cheaper, partly reversing the previous session’s rally while retaining weekly gains. The 2-year yield rose 1.9 basis points to 4.082%, the 5-year added 2.2 basis points to 4.207%, the 10-year increased 1.9 basis points to 4.481% and the 30-year edged 1.2 basis points higher to 4.968%. The 10-year real yield was almost unchanged at 2.151%, while the breakeven rose 2 basis points to 2.33%, showing that lower spot crude did not produce another decline in longer-run inflation compensation.

WTI fell 3.23% to $84.88 and Brent declined 3.37% to $87.33 as the US and Iran moved closer to an agreement over the Strait of Hormuz. European front ends rallied sharply, but the early Treasury bid faded as investors weighed realized inflation pressure, resilient US activity and substantial odds of another Fed increase. Michigan sentiment improved to 48.9 and inflation expectations eased, though the 1-year reading remained elevated at 4.6%.

Equities advanced and volatility declined with oil, but a 3.05% rise in gold showed that geopolitical and inflation risks were not regarded as settled. After the 17:00 ET fixed-income cutoff, Pakistan’s prime minister announced an immediate cessation of military operations and a formal US-Iran signing planned for June 19. That announcement could not have caused Friday’s yield move; ceasefire implementation, the reopening of Hormuz and sustained energy flows remain the next tests.
